good adjective

classical

Traupman 322

bonus, bona, bonum

adjective, first and second declension; comparative melior, superlative optimus · Declension on Wiktionary

good (also morally)

The general word, of things, people and conduct. “Be good to” is bonus esse + dat. (vīcīnīs bonus estō, Cato Agr. 4).

Other words

  • bonitās, bonitātis f. — goodness, kindness

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Traupman 153 · Declension on Wiktionary

  • probus, proba, probum — good, upright (morally)

    also used · classical · Traupman 322 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Good in character, honest (see moral).

  • rēctus, rēcta, rēctum — right, sound (of advice, a judgement)

    also used · classical · Traupman 322 · Declension on Wiktionary

  • serēnus, serēna, serēnum — fine, clear (of weather)

    also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 16.9.2: caelō serēnō; Traupman 322 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Of the sky and weather: caelō serēnō, in fine weather (see clear sky).

Examples

  • vīcīnīs bonus estō; familiam nē sīverīs peccāre

    be good to the neighbours; don’t let your household misbehaveCato Agr. 4

  • Bonum signum nūntiās, jam sentiēbam ēsuriem.

    That’s good news: I was beginning to feel hungry.Cord. Coll. IV 33

See also well-behaved, moral, bad, clear sky, great.
